## Game servers

**What it does.** Sells per-game tiers (RAM/slots/price) that provision a VPS from a game OS template,
then exposes game-specific settings, SFTP access and auto-update.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Game servers                                        [ + New server ]  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  mc-survival    Minecraft (paper)   4 GB / 20 slots    RUNNING          │
│    51.79.162.96:25565      [Console] [SFTP] [Settings] [Update now]    │
│                                                                        │
│  SETTINGS — Minecraft (paper)                                          │
│    Difficulty      ( ) peaceful (•) easy ( ) normal ( ) hard           │
│    Max players     [ 20 ]                                              │
│    PVP             [x] enabled                                         │
│    MOTD            [ Welcome to the server!            ]               │
│    [x] Auto-update the server every 6 hours                            │
│    [  Save & apply  ]                                                  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Entry points.** `GamePlan` model (`prisma/schema.prisma:777`) layers a game tier on a base `Plan`
plus a game `OsTemplate`; 14 tiers seeded in `prisma/seed-gameplans.ts:32-55`, all `termMonths: 1`,
flat-priced (no term discounts). Admin CRUD `/admin/game-plans`, actions
`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-gameplans.ts`. Ordering `orderGameServer`.

**Renewal pricing is the one thing to get right here.** A game server carries **both** a `planId` and
a `gamePlanId`, and it is sold at the game plan's flat price. `renewalCharge`
(`lib/renewal-charge.ts:43`) branches on `isGame` (`:47`) for the term (`:48`), the price (`:54`) and
the **invoice label** (`:66`) — so a game server's invoice names the game plan, not the base VPS.
Anything that quotes or charges a renewal must go through that function; a second formula over
`plan.priceCents` would have billed `minecraft-mm8w85` $8.99 for a $4.99 product. The incident is
recorded at `:22`. See the Renewals chapter.

Config schema and validation `/opt/nxeon/lib/game-config.ts`; apply worker
`/opt/nxeon/worker/game-config.ts`; update worker `/opt/nxeon/worker/game-update.ts` +
`/opt/nxeon/lib/game-update-verify.ts`, with a 6-hourly sweep (`worker/index.ts:1171`). Feature flag
`feature_game_servers`. Tests: `/opt/nxeon/test/games.test.ts`, `/opt/nxeon/test/game-update.test.ts`.

**Honest note — one live, one closed.**

**1. Settings apply is switched off in production, and the UI still promises it works.**
`worker/game-config.ts:39`: `REAL_APPLY_ENABLED = !SANDBOX && process.env.ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG === "1"`.
`ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG` is **not** set in `/opt/nxeon/.env`. The good change (commit `c6e156e`) is that
the simulated branch now **throws** outside sandbox (`:86-90`) instead of lying:

> *"Game settings could not be applied: real application is switched off on this server
> (ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG is not set), so nothing was written to the game … your settings are NOT in
> effect."*

The comment at `:71-85` records what it replaced: production had no flag, so every real customer
request fell through, stamped an `_appliedAt` marker, and notified *"Game settings applied on
`<hostname>`"* with the `(sandbox)` qualifier suppressed — because `SANDBOX` is false on production.
The customer changed their difficulty or slot count and was told it was applied.

So the lie is gone, but **the feature is non-functional today** and the customer-facing copy has not
caught up: `components/customer/GameSettings.tsx:73` says *"Changes are queued and applied to the
server"* and `:127` says *"Settings queued for apply."* Even on the real path, nothing reads back —
`worker/game-config.ts:118-165` writes files over SSH and notifies "applied" without confirming the
write landed or the service restarted, and `:138-145` writes the `_appliedAt` marker even when
`outcome.ok === false`.

**2. Auto-update used to be unable to fail — closed.** The remote command was
`set -e; ${steam}${restart}; true`: the steamcmd update was `|| true` and skipped entirely if
`steamcmd` was absent, every restart branch was `|| true`, and the whole command ended `; true`. It
**could not exit non-zero**, so for every server with `autoUpdate: true` the handler always resolved
and always fired *"The latest server update was applied and the service was restarted"* — unattended,
every 6 hours, regardless of what actually happened on the box.

The command builder, the output parser and the verdict now live in
`/opt/nxeon/lib/game-update-verify.ts`, and the design rules are stated where they can be enforced
(`:60-77`):

- **No `set -e`, no trailing `; true`, no `|| true`.** Control flow is explicit and the exit status is
  irrelevant — **the markers are the contract** (`updateCommand`, `:78`), so a truncated or dropped
  connection is detectable by the absence of `NXGU:END` rather than indistinguishable from success.
- **steamcmd's own exit code is not trusted** — it is unreliable and frequently non-zero on a
  perfectly good update — so its success line is matched instead and the code reported alongside.
- *"No unit matched"* is an outcome that gets emitted, not a branch that gets swallowed.
- The post-restart state is polled and reported verbatim; `active` is the only thing called success.

`parseGameUpdateOutput` (`:163`) and `judgeGameUpdate` (`:213`) turn that into a verdict.
`worker/game-update.ts:145` throws on `!verdict.ok`, which puts the reason in `Job.error` and the
admin job list, and the success notification at `:160` uses the verdict's own title and body. Guarded
by `test/game-update.test.ts`.

## Build with AI — Claude Code on every VPS

Done. Summary:

**Custom server option** — already exists platform-wide, no code change needed: `lib/custom-plan.ts` `createCustomGamePlan` (rates in `lib/custom-plan-pricing.ts`), wired into every game's deploy flow via `lib/actions-custom-plan.ts`. Confirmed live in `components/customer/GameDeployWizard.tsx`.

**4-tier ladder — shipped to STAGING only, verified:**
- New idempotent seed script `/root/nxeon-worktrees/game-plans/prisma/seed-gameplans-4tier.ts` (upserts by deterministic `gp4t-*` ids; run twice — 53 created then 53 updated, confirming idempotency).
- Ran against `nxeon_staging` (`DATABASE_URL` from `/opt/nxeon-staging/.env`). Verified via independent SQL: **47/47 families now have exactly 4 active `GamePlan` tiers** (188 rows total, up from 120).
- Also backfilled the 5 families staging was missing entirely (dayz, armareforger, cs16, ets2, ats) — created their `OsTemplate` rows (copied verbatim from prod) and their 3 existing tiers verbatim, before adding each one's new 4th tier.
- **Production untouched**: confirmed 135 active `GamePlan` rows unchanged, 0 rows with `gp4t-*` ids in prod.
- Every existing tier's id/specs/price is byte-identical to before — only new rows were inserted.

**Design method** (full detail + all 47 per-family tables in `/root/nxeon-competitive/plan-ladders.md`): each new tier sized from that family's own fitted player→resource curve (`lib/game-player-recommend.ts`, the same one the live wizard/custom-plan slider use), priced by linear-regression-extrapolating that family's own existing $/GB curve, with two guardrails added after catching real problems: (1) an entry tier's $/GB is floored at the smallest existing tier's own rate (7 families' raw fits went economically backwards — cheaper-per-GB-when-smaller — before this), (2) a top tier's disk never shrinks vs. the existing top (the generic curve undershot several families' real disk needs). Player counts on new tiers are recommendations, matching the family's own player-count convention.

**Judgment-call exceptions** (documented in §6 of the proposal):
- **CS2** gets two tiers *above* its ceiling instead of entry+top — a 1GB entry would sit below Source 2's real floor.
- **ATS/ETS2** — both hard-cap at 8 players in-engine, so their 4th tier is RAM/disk headroom ("Heavy Modded Convoy") at the same player count, not more players.
- **Core Keeper** — same headroom framing; its curve is a documented placeholder.
- **Icarus, Sunkenland** — hand-sized rather than curve-computed; the generic formula either tied the existing top tier's RAM (icarus) or implied a ~3x price jump for a small player increase (sunkenland) — both are in `lib/game-player-recommend.ts`'s own "Wave 3 SCAFFOLD... must be re-fit" flagged set.
- Abiotic Factor and Dragonwilds are also flagged-placeholder families but their computed numbers already matched organic progression, so no override was needed.

**UI wording fix** (matches the owner's "recommendations, not limits" ask): `components/customer/GameDeployWizard.tsx` said "Up to N player slots"/"Up to N players" in 3 places (plan list, review row, payment line item) — the literal hard-cap language, while `components/nx/DeployView.tsx` already said "Sized for ~N players" for the same number. Reworded the 3 spots to match; pure copy change, no behavior change. Flagged (via `spawn_task`, id `task_b28cc13b`) ~100 more instances of "N player slots" in `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`'s per-game marketing bullets as an out-of-scope follow-up.

**Docs**: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` updated (a "Game plan 4-tier ladder..." dated entry in §Change history, plus a note in the "Game servers" reference section); `ROADMAP.md` got a new queued item for the production apply, pending owner sign-off.

**Important — shared worktree note**: `/root/nxeon-worktrees/game-plans` had substantial *pre-existing uncommitted* changes from other work when I started (`components/nx/CustomServer.tsx` new file, plus edits to `order.tsx`, `order-types.ts`, `DeployView.tsx`, `actions-custom-plan.ts`, and some contact-page files — looks like a parallel effort building the Nexion-portal custom-server UI). I did **not** touch, commit, or evaluate those files — my commit (`a50a1edf5d` on `feat/game-plans-custom`) contains only the 4 files I actually authored: `prisma/seed-gameplans-4tier.ts`, `components/customer/GameDeployWizard.tsx`, `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`, `ROADMAP.md`. That other work is still sitting uncommitted in the worktree exactly as I found it.

**Production apply** (not run, needs owner price sign-off first): `DATABASE_URL="<prod>" npx tsx prisma/seed-gameplans-4tier.ts` — one line, stated in the proposal.
